### 1. Identification of Significantly Longer Cases Based on the timestamps, here are the total resolution times per case: | Case | Total Resolution Time | Status | |------|----------------------|--------| | 103 | 1h 20m | ✅ Fast | | 101 | 2h 15m | ✅ Fast | | 102 | 25h 10m | 🔴 Slow | | 104 | 24h 10m | 🔴 Slow | | 105 | 49h 05m | 🔴🔴 Very Slow | **Cases 102, 104, and 105** are significantly slower than 101 and 103. Case 105 is the worst performer at nearly 2 days. --- ### 2. Root Cause Analysis of Performance Issues By mapping the elapsed time between each activity, clear bottlenecks emerge: | Gap Between Activities | Case 101 | Case 102 | Case 103 | Case 104 | Case 105 | |---------------------------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------| | Receive → Triage | 10m | 25m | 5m | 40m | 10m | | Triage → Assign | 10m | 30m | 15m | 30m | 25m | | Assign → Investigate/Escalate | 40m | 2.5h | 15m | 3.5h | 10m | | Investigate → Resolve | 1h | **~19h** | 30m | **~19h** | **~19h** | | Escalation Handling (if any) | N/A | 2.5h | N/A | N/A | **28h** | **Key Root Causes:** 1. **Weekend/Non-Working Hours Downtime:** March 1, 2024 is a Friday. The consistent **~19-hour gap** between `Investigate Issue` and `Resolve Ticket` in cases 102, 104, and 105 falls entirely on Saturday and Sunday. Tickets sit idle when staff are offline, artificially inflating cycle time. 2. **Escalation Handoff Bottlenecks:** Cases 102 and 105 required escalation to Level-2. Case 105 shows a **28-hour delay** between escalation and the resumption of investigation, indicating L2 agent unavailability, queue congestion, or inefficient knowledge/context transfer. 3. **Pre-Investigation Queue Delays:** Cases 102 and 104 experienced **2.5–3.5 hour waits** between assignment and the start of active investigation. This suggests manual routing inefficiencies, agent overload, or lack of prioritization rules. 4. **Complex/Unresolved Investigations:** Even after investigation resumes, slow cases take ~19 hours to resolve vs. ~1 hour in fast cases. This points to either higher technical complexity, inadequate L1 diagnostics forcing escalations, or L2 resolution inefficiencies. --- ### 3. How These Factors Increase Cycle Times & Recommendations #### 🔍 Why These Factors Drag Down Performance - **Non-Value-Added Waits:** Idle time during weekends or pre-investigation queues adds zero value to the customer but consumes SLA/compliance clock time. - **Escalation Friction:** Handoffs require context rebuilding, re-prioritization, and bandwidth allocation. Without clear ownership or SLAs, escalated tickets stall. - **Compounding Delays:** A delay at one stage (e.g., weekend pause) often merges with downstream delays (e.g., L2 backlog), turning manageable tickets into multi-day cases. #### 💡 Actionable Recommendations | Bottleneck | Recommended Fix | |------------|-----------------| | **Weekend/After-Hours Gaps** | • Adopt **calendar-aware SLAs** (measure time in working hours, not clock hours).
• Implement **asynchronous resolution** (e.g., automated diagnostics, self-service knowledge base, or weekend on-call rotation) to maintain progress. | | **Escalation Delays** | • Set strict **L2 handoff SLAs** (e.g., acknowledge within 15m, begin investigation within 2h).
• Improve **L1 triage accuracy** with decision trees/AI to reduce unnecessary escalations.
• Use **structured handoff templates** to eliminate context loss. | | **Pre-Investigation Waits** | • Deploy **auto-assignment** based on skill, load, and ticket type.
• Implement **queue monitoring & alerting** for tickets waiting >30m.
• Introduce **tiered routing** so routine issues bypass manual triage. | | **Long Resolution Phases** | • Conduct **root cause analysis** on tickets requiring ~19h resolution.
• Equip L1 with **advanced diagnostic tools** to resolve complex issues earlier.
• Establish **L2 capacity planning** to ensure dedicated bandwidth for escalated cases. | **Expected Impact:** Implementing calendar-aware SLAs, automating triage/routing, and stabilizing escalation workflows can realistically reduce average cycle time by **60–75%**, bring weekend stalls into compliance, and improve First Contact Resolution (FCR) and customer satisfaction (CSAT).
